notes.1ai: Many candidates were not accurate enough when labelling the different features , particularly the cell wall. Label lines should not have arrow heads. The plasmid was often identified incorrectly.
notes.1aii: Many candidates did not read the question correctly and gave features of a bacterial cell e.g. , cell wall rather than characteristics of living organisms shown by bacteria.
notes.1bi: Most candidates answered correctly but s ome were confused by the first part, stating infected ‘ with gonorrhoea ’.
notes.1bii: M any candidates found the calculation demanding.
notes.1ci: Candidates needed to look very carefully at the leaf cross - section and at the different tissues. The shape of the cell should help identify the cell . The end point of each line is important, as epidermis and spongy mesophyll are close together. The line for D labels the cuticle , not the epidermis.
notes.1cii: Many correctly named the xylem and phloem .
notes.1di: Candidates should take notice of the description of images and diagrams. If it is a picture of a leaf, then answers about skin or blood are not suitable. Few candidates identified the guard cell.
notes.1dii: Good attempts were made to describe how this cell adapts the leaf for photosynthesis. Some candidates confused which gases were entering or leaving the stomata.
notes.2a: Many candidates selected the correct conclusions.
notes.2bi: Although most candidates understood that the seed needed water for germination, many thought the seed would be photosynthesising so gave carbon dioxide as a requirement. Many confused growth with germination.
notes.2bii: Candidates predicted that the seed would still germinate, but did not notice that the higher, optimal temperature would result in faster germination. The first investigation was at 10 ° C, so germination at the middle of the range of temperature should be faster.
notes.2c: A well answered question. A few candidates gave ‘ photo trophic ’ in error, rather than phototropic. Better responses described the plant root grow ing into the soil or towards gravity or the centre of the Earth. A common error was to state that plants grow on the ground which was not sufficiently clear for the mark to be awarded .
notes.3a: Candidates need to be careful with their description of an acid. Whereas highly acidic is correct, high pH describes an alkali.
notes.3bi: Most candidates calculated the percentage correctly.
notes.3bii: It was important to select the contaminated water section for the calculation. A few candidates used their own calculation from 3 (b)(i) .
notes.3c: Candidates showed a good understanding of hygiene and prevention of infection.
notes.3d: Most candidates gave correct answers. Body defence means defence by the body , not how we can protect the body.
notes.3e: This proved to be a challenging question as most candidates did not recognise it as a bacterial cell, but as a plant cell.
notes.4a: Many candidates were not able to give the word equation for photosynthesis. Some gave the respiration equation. A few candidates tried to write a symbol equation. If this was completely correct , marks were awarded . (b )( i)(ii) Many candidates were able to name the pigment but not the structure. Other candidates got them the wrong way round.
notes.4bi: Few candidates knew which food items are high in i ron.
notes.4bii: The question ask ed for the roles of blood clotting. Some candidates described how blood clots or how blood travels around the body.
notes.5a: Most candidates identified the ribs and diaphragm but not the intercostal muscle.
notes.5bi: Candidates need to be careful with naming parts, some confused bronchi with bronchioles.
notes.5bii: Candidates need to understand the different parts of the breathing system and how they are connected.
notes.5ci: Candidates were asked to identify the direction of carbon dioxide movement. M any candidates selected arrows for oxygen.
notes.5cii: A few candidates described how gases are exchanged, rather than the features of the alveoli that enable efficient gas exchange .
notes.5di: Most knew the word equation for aerobic respiration.
notes.5dii: Many candidates misread the question and gave a type of cell, rather than a structure within a cell.
notes.6a: This question on variation was g enerally well answered.
notes.6bi: Candidates found this a demanding question. Many just repeated the first stage (that was given in the question) . Some candidates clearly did not understand the term drought tolerance, others suggested giving the plants plenty of water. The question needed a description of selective breeding.
notes.6bii: F ew candidates correctly stated selective breeding , many saying mutation or adaptation.
notes.6ci: Most answered correctly although some gave both parts of the name or just the species name.
notes.6cii: Many were awarded full marks on this question. A common mistake was to identify the yellow - spotted flower plant as Bb but then go on to complete the P unnet square correctly.
notes.6d: Most candidates correctly identified the enzyme.
notes.7ai: The scientific name for elephant wa s given above the photograph . Most candidates selected the correct genus. A few gave the species name.
notes.7aii: Most answered correctly, although a few gave features that were not visible .
notes.7bi: Some candidates could identify the correct answer.
notes.7bii: ,(iii) The concept of trophic levels was not well understood with very few able to interpret the food web correctly.
notes.7biii: Most c andidates correctly identified a producer.
notes.7biv: Most candidates knew that i nsect s are arthropod s .
notes.7bv: Most candidates were able to construct a food chain using organisms from the food web. Very few gave a chain using other animals.
notes.7bvi: Most answers were descriptions of a food web rather than an ecosystem .
notes.7c: Only a few correct responses were seen.
notes.7d: Most could give at least one way in which endangered species could be conserved , although most thought this question was still about the food web earlier in the question.
notes.1c: Lots of candidates used the word immune rather than resistant.
notes.1d: This question was g enerally well answered although some candidates stated ‘ use protection ’ rather than giving appropriate examples. Do not have sexual relations with lots of people was a common answer which did gain credit as it is too general.
notes.2ai: Most candidates were able to correctly identify the phloem and xylem, although a few candidates got them the wrong way round.
notes.2aii: Very few correctly identified the cortex cells. Incorrect answers included all parts of a plant.
notes.2b: Very few candidates gave an answer which mentioned structure or support. Most candidates stat ed transport of water but many also stat ed transport of sucrose.
notes.2ci: Some candidates put root rather than root hair.
notes.2cii: This question was g enerally well answered but several stat ed absorption rather than osmosis .
notes.2ciii: Most candidates knew that the structure increases the surface area .
notes.2d: Most candidates knew that diffusion involved substances moving down a concentration gradient but many also thought that this required energy.
notes.2e: Few candidates were able to name mitochondria as the site of aerobic respiration, instead stat ing various plant structures.
notes.3ai: Few candidates were able to name the adrenal gland, most offering adrenaline or kidney in stead . Many kn e w that that the testes secrete testosterone.
notes.3aii: Very few candidates were able to describe a hormone. Those that did kn o w it was a chemical and was transported by the blood were often confused about where it acts.
notes.3aiii: Most knew that hormones act more slowly than the nervous system.
notes.3b: Most gained all four marks, although some were confused about the diameter of the pupil increasing to let in more light.
notes.4ci: V ery few candidates were awarded full marks. It wa s important to read the question carefully as a whole number wa s asked for.
notes.4cii: This question wa s a describe and explain so it is important that both parts of the question are answered in order to gain full marks. It was quite well answered with most candidates able to describe the graph , although some did not recognise that this question was about photosynthesis.
notes.5ai: Most candidates correctly identified the ovary . F ewer could identify the site s of fertilisation and implantation .
notes.5aii: Many candidates could not identify structure N as the cervix. Most correctly identified structure L as the uterus.
notes.5b: Candidates found this a demanding question. S ome candidates suggested it was large, had a large surface area or it was stationary. Some gave the features of a sperm.
notes.7e: M any candidates gave answers that were too vague and could not be credited.
